Depraved Homosexual: He takes Snake and Chief Wiggum captive for the implied purpose of raping them in "22 Short Films About Springfield."Herman:As soon asZedgets here, the party will begin. Evil Cripple: He's missing his right arm. As for the other part, he's a crook who's taken captives, attempted murder andscams people for phony antiques.

characters.name: Akira Kurosawa
characters.description: A Japanese restaurant owner and martial arts instructor. Demoted to Extra: With many of the non-white characters being recast after the murder of George Floyd, Akira has yet to be recast and he has remained a silent background character. Even before then, his appearances had become scarce. Famous-Named Foreigner: Named after thefamous director. Japanese Politeness: Banning Homer from his restaurant for being aCaustic Criticwould be rude.Killing him is fine, though.

characters.name: Mayor Joe Quimby
characters.description: Springfield's mayor and head of a rich and politically influential clan. Known for his womanizing, general corruption and for changing his political stance at the drop of a hat if he thinks it will increase his popularity with the voters. The Alcoholic: In Italy, his picture illustrates "Drinko Drivo". Bastard Begetter: He's a sleazy womanizer who's had countless extra-marital affairs, and as a result fathered an unknown number of illegitimate children. In one episode alone he was facing no less than 27 separate Paternity suits, with him still trying to deny the children were his despite the blatant resemblance. Card-Carrying Jerkass: He is not only aSleazy Politicianbut he shamelessly embraces the fact that he is one. Catchphrase: "Vote Quimby!"

characters.name: State Comptroller Atkins
characters.description: The comptroller of whatever state Springfield is in. Tuckerization: His name is a reference to producers' assistant Jacqueline Atkins.

characters.name: Judge Roy Snyder
characters.description: One of the main judges in Springfield. He is usually actually very good at his job. Bunny-Ears Lawyer: A good judge for the most part, but has a strange preoccupation with a clown desk figurine. First-Name Basis: With Bart, to show that he is familiar with the delinquent. Bart would have been sent to juvie if Snyder wasn't that lenient toward him. Inconsistent Coloring: He appeared as white (that is, yellow) in his first appearance inthe first seasonand later appeared as black ina season three episode. Unlike in the cases of Smithers and Lou, he flip-flopped back and forth between the two skin colors, appearing with yellow skin as late asseason ten. Since then, he has always been black. No Celebrities Were Harmed: His overall look and persona is loosely based on Robert Bork (a fairly infamous figure at the time, having recently been rejected as a Supreme Court Justice).

characters.name: Judge Constance Harm
characters.description: Occasionally replacing theReasonable Authority FigureJudge Snyder, Judge Harm is a cruelHanging Judgethrough and through. Disproportionate Retribution: A lot. One example would be in "On a Clear Day, I Can't See My Sister", when she increases the distance on how far Bart has to be from Lisa after Bart insults her. Hanging Judge: To give one example of how harsh she can be, in one episode she retracted Homer's driving license for driving his car off a dock (because it had too many accessories installed) doing so by cutting up the license, chopping the pieces up with a miniature guillotine, feeding what was left to a pair of dogs, and then ordering the court officers to "Burn their poop!". She also allowed Lisa (a minor with no consent from her parents) to file a restraining order on her own brother and increased the order's range when Bart (stupidly) insulted her figure and marriage during the appeal. Jerkass: Big time. It doesn't help that she's played byJane Kaczmarek. She enjoys creating cruel and unusual punishments for criminals in her court. Jerkass Has a Point: Despite being a harshJerkass, she does rightfully call out Homer for being a bad father.

characters.name: Lionel Hutz
characters.description: A severely incompetent but determined lawyer, who usually works for the Simpson family. 30 Minutes, or It's Free!: In a deleted scene, he apparently has a "cases won in thirty minutes, or your pizza's free!" policy.Hutz:(Upon being informed that the case was won in his absence) Well that's okay, the box was empty! Affably Evil: He's sleazy and corrupt as all get out, but he also has a cheerful, happy-go-lucky attitude. He also tries to be helpful to his legal clients - usually the Simpson - even if he's only motivated by greed. The key word being tries, given his incompetence. The Alcoholic: As implied in "Marge in Chains." He even argues his case before the court and is then informed he isn't wearing any pants. He's also seen drinking scotch at nine-thirty in the morning, which he justifies by claiming that he hasn't slept in days. In front of clients, no less. Ambulance Chaser: In "Bart Gets Hit By a Car", Homer says upon meeting him, "You were the guy chasing Bart's ambulance." Another time when he's meeting with Homer at his office, he hears a siren in the distance and looks like he's about to run after it before changing his mind and staying to deal with Homer.

characters.name: The Blue-Haired Lawyer
characters.description: Springfield's most prominent lawyer, known for his pasty face, blue hair, New York accent and nasal voice. Amoral Attorney: Although unlike most examples, he isn'toutright malevolent. Artistic License – Law: ARunning Gagis that he'll claim copyright infringement over things that are in the public domain, like Christmas carols. One Halloween episode has him making a solid legal document that would allow Burns to hunt people. Bullying a Dragon: He found out the hard way that trying to intimidate ex-Green Beret Seymour Skinnerwasn’t the best idea. Bunny-Ears Lawyer: Amoral, greedy and nasally sounding but he is the only competent lawyer in town and does win his cases often.

characters.name: Chief Clancy Wiggum
characters.description: Chief of Springfield Police Department, Chief Wiggum is portrayed as lazy, gluttonous, out of shape, incompetent (if not mildly corrupt) and dim-witted. Acrofatic: Like Homer, he can be surprisingly quick on his feet at times, catching up with and tackling Snake after a car crash and later managing to do a front flip off a roof even though he messed up the landing and got hurt. Adaptation Dye-Job: In the first seasons his hair was black, but then it was colored blue and remained so in subsequent episodes. Ambiguously Bi: He is clearly married to a woman and Ralph is his son and he visited burlesque houses, but he has some questionable subtext with his partner, Lou. He also seemed to be attracted to Peter and Homer during their carwash sting operation in the crossover. He also uttered this line in "Homer Alone" after being kissed repeatedly by Homer for finding Maggie:Chief Wiggum:(chuckles)Just don't do it again, ya big lug. Artistic License – Gun Safety: Parodied. He's known to misuse his gun in ways that would surely get him killed. Whenever itdoesgo off, it just barely misses him, which doesn't deter Wiggum in the slightest.

characters.name: Sergeant Lou and Officer Eddie
characters.description: Chief Wiggum's seconds-in-command. Lou is the more active of the duo, while Eddie really doesn’t do much except act as more firepower when Wiggum needs it. Absence Makes the Heart Go Yonder: After Lou and Amy divorced, Eddie began dating and sleeping with her. Ambiguously Bi: When Wiggum tells Eddie to direct traffic because he's the most graceful, Eddie makes flamboyant gestures while doing so and Wiggum comments "And that guy can't find a girlfriend, I'll never figure it out." However, Eddie is also mentioned to have slept with Lou's ex-wife. Butt-Monkey: Whenever Lou raises minor objections, he will usually get chewed out for complaining by Chief Wiggum. Eddie is the one who gets injured. Catchphrase: Lou says, "Uh, Chief?"

characters.name: Robert Underdunk Terwilliger, Jr., Ph.D. (Sideshow Bob)
characters.description: A man cursed to have both huge feet (standard floppy clown shoes fit himperfectly) and a natural hairstyle like a palm tree while also having a keen intellect, he was, while originally not interested in becoming a performer, coaxed into joining theKrusty the Clown Showwith the prospect of appealing to a huge audience of children with his own brand of edutainment. To his horror, though, his ideas were all ignored and he became the abused straight-man for Krusty's lowbrow slapstick. Jealousy and resentment eventually led to him framing Krusty and then assuming control over the show while Krusty was imprisoned, but Bart Simpson exposed him and sent him to prison. As a result, he carries a murderous grudge against both his former "partner" and the Simpson boy. Advertised Extra: Despite his enormous popularity and being added to the HD version of the opening introduced in Season 20, he's to date only made significant appearances in 16 of the show's more than 750 episodes (two of them being Treehouse of Horror episodes), with a handful of brief cameos elsewhere. Justified, due to him being technically voiced by a recurring guest star. Affably Evil: From time to time, he's portrayed in a more genuinely likable light. Of course, this doesn't stop him from being a ruthless criminal. Animalistic Abilities: In "The Man Who Grew Too Much", Sideshow Bob reveals he's been modifying his own DNA and now has, among other things, the strength of a Brahma bull, the thighs of a grasshopper, and the sonar of a killer whale. Anime Hair: He could be mistaken for a palm tree with the right dye.

characters.name: Chester Turley (Snake Jailbird)
characters.description: A recurring petty thug and crook, most often seen mugging people or holding up the Kwik-E-Mart. Ruthless and murderous, yet often portrayed with depths you wouldn't expect from a criminal of his ilk. Adventurer Archaeologist: He was formerly an idealisticIndiana Jones-type archaeologist, but became a thief. Affably Evil: When he's not being an active menace, he can actually be pretty polite. Animal Motif: He's themed around snakes, as shown by his name, alias, tattoo and car decoration of a cobra. InMarge Gamer, his in-game avatar is a snake and he even dresses as a snake inRevenge Is a Dish Best Served Three Times. Animal Theme Naming: He's a criminal themed around snakes.

characters.name: Nick Callahan
characters.description: A corrupt realtor and con man. Asshole Victim: He's mauled to death by an otter on a cocaine high in "The Yellow Lotus", but he's such a scumbag it's hard to feel sad. Back for the Dead: Twenty-seven years pass between his first appearance in "Realty Bites" and his second in "The Yellow Lotus". The latter episode sees himKilled Off for Real. Card-Carrying Villain: When Marge reminds Nick that she and Homer were the expecting couple he scammed ten years ago, he doesn't care, replying "Do youknowhow many pregnant women I have defrauded?" Catchphrase: "Boo-yah!"

characters.name: Marion Anthony "Fat Tony" D'Amico
characters.description: Street boss of the Springfield Mafia. According to "Donnie Fatso", Fat Tony died and was replaced by hisidentical cousin. Like Armin Tanzarian and Snowball II's death,don't expect this to come up again. Affably Evil: Despite being a ruthless mafia leader who has committed almost every crime under the sun, he's a genuinely polite person and is on good terms with most of the Simpson family, especially Marge. He's even part of the carpool that the Simpsons kids are part of. Ambiguously Bi: Tony had a wife (now deceased), but also expressed interest in Homer during the latter's time asThe Molefor the police. He described it as "heterosexual male friendship like the Greeks wrote about", which is an extremely ambiguous line. Ascended Extra: Another one of those characters that the writers expected to appear only once, but kept coming back. Back Up Twin: In Donnie Fatso, Fat Tony died and his cousin Fit Tony, who was identical in every way but build, took his place. Fit Tony quickly becomes Fat Tony due to overeating, essentially bringing Fat Tony back to life.

characters.name: Legs and Louie
characters.description: Fat Tony's associates. Back-Alley Doctor: Legs is apparently a mob doctor, and sews Homer's thumb back on in one episode. Lisa states that he's in for a long and agonizing recovery. Butt-Monkey: Louie is often put down upon by his fellow gangsters. Evil Counterpart: To Lou and Eddie: they either are or may as well be the only members of Fat Tony's gang as Lou and Eddie are the only cops besides Chief Wiggum. Louie in particular has a similar name to Lou and will either beThose Two Guyswith Legs or part of aStraight Man and Wise Guydue with their boss, depending on the needs of the episode. Expy: Of Frankie Carbone fromGoodFellas, according to the latter's actor (who unsuccessfully sued the producers ofThe Simpsons).

characters.name: Johnny Tightlips
characters.description: A mobster and an associate of Fat Tony. And no, he ain't tellin' you nothin'. Ascended Extra: He first appeared in a bit scene in "Bart the Murderer", went largely unused for the next 8 seasons, and was then reused for the gag below in "Insane Clown Poppy." Since then, he has become a semi-regular recurring character, often being shown as part of Fat Tony's entourage alongside Legs and Louie. The Comically Serious: The entire joke with this guy is that he's stoic and refuses to say anything useful even when it's counterproductive. In one scene, he insists there's a good reason for an assailant on him to not shoot him, but also that he refuses to spill the beans on why. Early Installment Character-Design Difference: He was much more tan in his first few appearances. Even Bad Men Love Their Mamas: He goes through his usual routine about whether or not his car's outside until 1. he learns it's being towed and 2. "Hey, my grandma's in there!"

characters.name: Frankie the Squealer
characters.description: A low-level member of the Springfield mafia and associate of Fat Tony. He is known, as his name suggests, for his indiscretion. Early Installment Character-Design Difference: He was more tan in his first appearance. Foil: To Johnny Tightlips, naturally, since he's addicted to ratting people out to the extent that it's impossible for him to keep his mouth shut. The Friend No One Likes: The rest of the mafia clearly don't like him but he never goes anywhere. Iron Butt-Monkey: One Halloween episode had the mafia shoot him to no effect due to Homer killing the Grim Reaper and temporarily prevented everyone from dying, while he calls his wife and tells her he'll be home late.

characters.name: Reverend Timothy Lovejoy
characters.description: The preacher at the church that the Simpsons family and the Flanders family attend. He really doesn't care much about his job or his "flock" at all, and can even be read as not actually being that religious. He's often no more reasonable on religious matters than Springfield's other religious characters — he just usually has ulterior motives, typically relating to increasing the money he gets from the church. It's revealed that his original caring nature and sincere drive to help his congregation was basically eroded by coming into contact with Ned Flanders and his fixation on being a "proper" Christian. Voiced byHarry Shearer. Badass Preacher: Has saved Homer's life on at least one occasion, as well as Flanders' in another occasion. The Bore: His sermons are so lackluster and boring, he has a sound effect generator to wake people up from them. Bunny-Ears Lawyer: He may be a quirky priest, but "Homer the Heretic" implies Lovejoy somehow knows the entire Bible by heart, or at least the Gospels, and can quote any specific verse he is asked. Other episodes similarly imply he has a great theological knowledge, much to his listeners' boredom. Butt-Monkey: His trains are always getting destroyed.

characters.name: Helen Lovejoy
characters.description: Reverend Lovejoy's snooping, interfering, gossipy busy-body of a wife. The Alcoholic: After intentionally spiting Lisa to make her angry at Bart, Helen declares she will reward herself with a box of wine. Ambiguous Gender Identity: The Parson tells Lovejoy he remembers back when her name was Harold, but she's also been depicted in flashbacks as a little girl. She and her husband also have a daughter, but there's been no indication of whether or not Helen gave birth to her. Ambiguously Bi: During her and Timothy's roleplaying in "Sky Police" she becomes very interested when she hears another woman at the door, asking Tim to send her in. Ambiguously Jewish: The Parson says he remembers her when her last name was Schwartzbaum.

characters.name: Ms. Albright
characters.description: Early Installment Character-Design Difference: In her first appearance, she had glasses, which never appeared again. Nice Girl: A kind woman and gentle teacher. Reasonable Authority Figure: Unlike Helen, Ms. Albright is usually friendly and tries to teach genuine lessons to the children she is with, the few times she punishes a child are justified as well, as they’re normally disruptive during her teachings.

characters.name: Dr. Julius Hibbert
characters.description: Unflappable family doctor to the Simpsons and a number of other Springfieldians. Voiced byHarry Shearer(1990-2021)/Kevin Michael Richardson(2021-present). All Men Are Perverts: Some episodes show he has a few fetishes and how he has an open marriage with his wife. In "In the Name of the Grandfather", he and his wife are among the small group of swingers approaching the hot tub. In "500 Keys", he once hosted a key party and invited Homer and Marge to it (who left immediately once they realisedwhata key party was). Despite this, he's still one of the more competent townsfolk of Springfield and more than capable of doing his job. Back-Alley Doctor: Zigzagged. While he is sometimes seen as a genuinely competent doctor, he does seem to have questionable practices. It's even implied that he might be practicing without a medical licence. Though whatever the case, he's always much more competent thanDr. Nick. Big Ol' Eyebrows: Is one of the few characters to have these. Black Republican: Shown attending meetings of the Republican party.

characters.name: Doctor Nick Riviera
characters.description: A quack physician with an exaggerated Hispanic accent. Voiced byHank Azaria. Afraid of Blood: Shown being squicked by blood while learning surgery. Also heard panicking about it and fainting on stages where he's a background character inThe Simpsons Wrestling. Ambiguously Evil: He seems nice and helpful, but he's willing to do some very immoral things and God help you if you depend on him for treatment. Back-Alley Doctor: In "King-Sized Homer"noteThe Season 7 episode where Homer purposely gains weight so he can work from home, he tells Bart that he went to Hollywood Upstairs Medical College (which sounds dubious), but in "Homer's Triple Bypass," there's a flashback that implies he went to a real university, though the only thing he remembers from his college days is going to a frat party and hitting on a hippie chick. He also has a "no questions asked" policy with his clients, to the point that he (and his staff) hasSeen It Allwhen it comes to crime-related injuries and tells a gut-shot Snake in one episode: "You don't have to lie tome! Save it for the police!" Bunny-Ears Lawyer: He may be a quack doctor, but he's agoodquack doctor—that is to say, while going to him for a legitimate medical treatment is practically a suicide attempt, if you'relookingfor someone whose morals are as murky as their medical accreditation, he's the man to get you what youwantin lieu of what youneedto the point of essentially being theSaul Goodmanof medical practitioners. In "22 Short Films About Springfield", this ends up saving his job when his performance review (with his accreditation on the line) is interrupted byGrampa Simpson barging in with a scalpelandspecifically demandinga quack doctor to listen to his complaints, STAT. The other more professional doctors are unable to get Grampa to listen, but Dr. Nick—being the only quack in the house—manages to get through to him and calm him down with a "treatment", at the same timesaving his accreditationby demonstrating justwhythe doctors

characters.name: Dr. Marvin Monroe
characters.description: A TV psychologist in Springfield. Voiced byHarry Shearer. Alliterative Name:MarvinMonroe Bus Crash: He was retired around the seventh season asno one on the crew (not even his voice actor, Harry Shearer, who found Monroe's gravelly voice a real strain on his vocal chords) liked the character. The "Marvin Monroe Memorial Hospital" is mentioned in "Who Shot Mr. Burns? (Part Two)" as a way of quietly implying the character had passed away offscreen. His death was confirmed duringthe 138th episode spectacular. This episode revealed the death in the form of a question: "What two popular Simpsons characters have died in the past year?", to which the answer was, "If you said Bleeding Gums Murphy and Dr. Marvin Monroe you were wrong;they were never popular." Later episodes almost make aRunning Gagout of it, with his gravestone being seen in "Alone Again, Natura-Diddily" and the Marvin Monroe Memorial Gymnasium appearing in "Bye Bye Nerdie".However... Promotion to Opening Titles: He gets added to the house pan shot in season 2. However, due to hisChuck Cunningham Syndrome, he gets removed in the HD intro. Reports of My Death Were Greatly Exaggerated: Several years later he spontaneously appears at Marge's book signing, buying a copy of her book,The Harpooned Heart. Marge, shocked to see him, exclaims that she hasn't seen him in years. Dr. Monroe explains:"Oh, I've been very sick."

characters.name: Kent Brockman
characters.description: The primary reporter for the local TV News channel. Voiced byHarry Shearer. Ambiguously Jewish: It is revealed that he changed his name from "Kenny Brockelstein" and he is seen wearing a Hebrew chai necklace in "Dog of Death", but he frequently attends Reverend Lovejoy's church and mentions his belief in the New TestamentBook of Revelationin "Marge on the Lam". The Comically Serious: Reports on the absurdities of Springfield with a completely straight face.Kent:At the heart of the strike is former student body president Lisa Simpson. Her brother had this to say:Bart:Lisa is a nut! She has a rubber butt! Every time she turns around, it goes putt putt!Kent:Indeed. But that rubber butt doesn't have much time for turning around these days; it's pointed squarely in the face of the administration. Deadpan Snarker: In the vein of a typical news anchor, he makes monotone quips about everything. Delusions of Local Grandeur: Kent Brockman is astrawman Republicanwho got the idea to foray into politics due to the long decades he's spent as a newsreader and anchorman of Springfield's TV News channel.

characters.name: Krusty the Clown
characters.description: The most famous celebrity in Springfield, due to being the host of the city's favorite children's entertainment program,The Krusty the Klown Show. Born Herschel Shmoikel Pinchas Yerucham Krustofsky, an Orthodox Jew, he was estranged from his Rabbi father due to his wanting to be a clown instead of following in his father's footsteps. Originally an optimistic fellow who just wanted to help people laugh, years in the ugly reality of showbusiness have left him grizzled, sarcastic, jaded and indifferent, striving only to make as much money as possible. Voiced byDan Castellaneta. Acrofatic: He looks just as fat as Homer, but he frequently performs acrobatic tricks and flips during his shows. Alter Kocker: Is either on his way to this trope or already there,Depending on the Writer. Brilliant, but Lazy: He's capable of brilliant physical comedy and has demonstrated a knack for subversive humor. He even used to be a thoughtful and incisive interviewer. It's just that he became used to the trappings of fame over the years and prefers making loads of cash by licensing his name and likeness. Butt-Monkey: Despite being a celebrity (although how big of one he isdepends on the writer; see below), if Krusty's backstory is anything to go by, he often found himself the victims ofDisproportionate RetributionandGeorge Jetson Job Security. Such cases include being fired for22 yearsjust because a pair of stage shutters wouldn't open, pissing him off and making him start using language that wasn't acceptable on TV at the time, or getting his bus pass revoked for drinking a soda.

characters.name: Melvin Van Horne (Sideshow Mel)
characters.description: Krusty's sidekick on his TV show, a replacement for Sideshow Bob (who was arrested after attempting to frame Krusty the Clown by robbing the Kwik-E-Mart), Melvin Van Horne plays the part of an inarticulate caveman on stage, but is actually a very refined, dignified intellectual in his private life. Voiced byDan Castellaneta. Always Someone Better: Apparently, Krusty told him that he could never live up to the comedic genius of his predecessor, Sideshow Bob, something he complains about when the two meet for the first time. Ambiguous Gender Identity: In "Burger Kings", when Krusty's LGBTQBLT campaign is failing, he asks Mel for advice, since he's "three of those letters"… whatever that means. Given that Mel has been shown to crossdress, Krusty, in his usual ignorance, could be referring to that. Ambiguously Bi: If Krusty's comment on Mel from above doesn't refer to his gender identity then it could also refer to his sexual orientation. However he's only ever shown having attraction to women and has been married to one. Awful Wedded Life: He doesNOThave a good relationship with his wife, Barbara. It eventually culminates with her leaving him inThe Nightmare After Krustmas.

characters.name: Mr. Teeny
characters.description: Krusty's pet monkey who also acts as one of his sideshows as well as his chauffeur. Voiced byDan Castellaneta. Amplified Animal Aptitude: Given that he can drive Krusty's limo... (the comics also have him be Krusty's agent, which goespoorly). Cigar Chomper: Often seen puffing away on a cigar, presumably because seeing a monkey smoke is just funny. Legacy Character: Multiple episodes outright state that there have been multiple Mr. Teenys over the years, some Krusty remembers more favorably than others.Krusty:I haven't cried like this since the third Mr. Teeny died... (speaking to the current Mr Teeny) You couldn't hold a candle to him! (points to a taxidermied monkey on the wall marked "Mr Teeny") Neither could you! (points to the taxidermied Mr Teeny II) You were okay, you got me broads." Non-Human Sidekick: To Krusty.

characters.name: Rainier Luftwaffe Wolfcastle
characters.description: An Austrian who moved to Springfield and became an action movie star, Rainier Wolfcastle is legendary for the over-the-top nature of his movies and his bad acting. Voiced byHarry Shearer. The Ahnold: Of the man the trope is named after no less. He is one of the best known examples and currently the image on the trope page. In addition, his early work in pornography is a likely reference toSylvester Stallone. Bad "Bad Acting": Part and parcel of his archetype. Whenever he isn't shouting, his tone of voice can best be described as "reading his lines off cue cards." Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: There's been a few quick gags showcasing he's more vile than he looks, such as acting chummy with Krusty when the latter says out loud that he's an anti-Semite (instead of a "self-hating Jew",It's a Long Story) and his appearances as a member of the Springfield Republican Party. He also admitted outright that his father was a Nazi (a reference toGustav Schwarzenegger) and he's implied to be a sympathizer. Bond One-Liner: Is fond of these both in his movies and in person.

characters.name: TroyMcClure
characters.description: An aging actor who starred in an incredibly wide variety of B-movies, short-lived TV shows, and other projects (like telethons, funerals, medical education films, infomercials, self-help videos, TV retrospectives, Broadway shows, and automated welcome messages for museums, airports, and Nordstrom department store), who frequently reminds people of the works he's been in and clings to his stardom. Voiced byPhil Hartman. The Alcoholic: A severe one, according to "Bart's Inner Child". He used to be a fifty-a-day man.Troy: "Sweet liquor eases the pain." Bestiality Is Depraved: His career was killed after rumors spread that he does "weird things" to fish, including an indecent act he did at the local aquarium. His fish fetish is so bad, he brings a new, disgustingly literal meaning to the phrase, "sleeping with the fishes". Blind Without 'Em: Pretty much blind without his glasses, but he refuses to wear them. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: All of Hartman's characters were retired after his death, as production thought it would be in poor taste to simply replace him (the fact that his children would be watching was often cited). On very rare occasions, they will turn up in the background, though.

characters.name: Drederick Tatum
characters.description: A Mike Tyson-esque boxer, complete with a Don King-esque promoter named Lucius Sweet. Was from Springfield, and hated it. He stated in an interview that, "If you ever see me back in Springfield, you know I fucked up bad."note"fucked" was bleeped outVoiced byHank Azaria(1991-2022)/Jay Pharoah(2022-present). Badass in a Nice Suit: Usually wears a suit when he's not in the ring, and is very imposing and formidable. Beware the Nice Ones: Do NOT make him angry. Apparently the reason he was incarcerated was because he pushed his own mother down the stairs. We don't know why he did it, though when asked if he regretted doing so he confirmed that if he could do it all over again, "[he] would certainly reconsider it." Then he said he will make orphans of Homer's children. The Dreaded: Once stopped a full-blown prison riot from his cell by telling the rioters "Hey guys, come on, shut up!" while eating, and without raising his voice. The rioters promptly complied, immediately returning to their cells, and even a guard is shown to apologize to him. Early Installment Character-Design Difference: In Tatum's first few appearances he looked a lot different than he does now, e.g. he had no beard, a more snout-ish nose (like Chief Wiggum) and his hair was more flat.

characters.name: Chespirito (Bumblebee Man)
characters.description: A Latino entertainer for Channel Ocho. In his sitcom, he dresses in a bumblebee costume and performs slapstick comedy. Voiced byHank Azaria(1992-2020)/Eric Lopez(2020-present)/Humberto Vélez(¡The Fall Guy-Yi-Yi!only). Amusing Injuries: What his profession is all about. In¡The Fall Guy-Yi-Yi!, it starts to become too much for him to bear until he gets the idea to hire Homer as his own stuntman. Butt-Monkey: A lot of things go wrong for this man. For example, “22 Short Films about Springfield” sees him lose his wife and his house in only a few minutes. Captain Ersatz: OfEl Chapulín Colorado. Both are Latinos dressed in an insect costume (a grasshopper in the case ofEl Chapulín Colorado,chapulínmeaning "grasshopper" in Mexican Spanish) who star in a comedy show heavily based on slapstick comedy. Some of the props used by the Bumblebee Man, such as a giant mousetrap, were actually used inEl Chapulín Colorado. The show's producers say that that the character was conceived after noticing that whenever they watched Telemundo,El Chapulín Coloradowas always on. Some supplentary material gives his last name as "Chespirito", which happens to be the pseudonym used byEl Chapulín Coloradocreator and performer Roberto Gómez Bolaños. Catchphrase: His catchphrases of choice are typically "¡Ay, ay, ay, no me gusta!" ("I don't like it!"), "¡Ay, ay, ay, no es bueno!" ("That's not good!") and "¡Ay, Dios no me ama!" ("God doesn't love me!").

characters.name: Captain Lance Murdock
characters.description: A daredevil performer who does death-defying stunts. Voiced byDan Castellaneta. Amusing Injuries: He gets a lot of these, and is usually in traction when he's not performing a stunt. Butt-Monkey: Every single one of his appearances sees him suffering some sort of horrendous injury. Iron Butt-Monkey: When he's not in traction in the hospital, he's suffering gruesome injuries that land him there. Made of Iron: He's broken every bone in his body throughout his career.

characters.name: Bill and Marty
characters.description: TheDJduo for Springfield's KBBL station. Voiced byDan CastellanetaandHarry Shearer. Dumbass DJ: Marty especially. He keeps playing "The Monster Mash" by Bobby Pickett on days like Valentine's Day and Bill refers to him as dead weight when he makes an awful pun. Those Two Guys: They're never seen apart from one another.

characters.name: Booberella (real name: Barbara Jane Lelavinsky)
characters.description: An ample-chested vampire-looking woman and a local TV personality in Springfield. Voiced byTress MacNeille. Big-Breast Pride: She constantly tries to make sure her TV audience is staring at her breasts. Bob from Accounting: Not her, but her father Bill is in the Accounts dept. at the power plant. Eerie Pale-Skinned Brunette: Her skin is a much paler shade than most characters. It's probably makeup to make her look vampire-ish. Horror Host: Being a parody of Elvira, she fulfills this role onTVin-universe.

characters.name: Ernst and Gunter
characters.description: A German duo of animal performers. Voiced byHarry ShearerandHank Azaria. No Celebrities Were Harmed: They're based on performers, Siegfried and Roy.

characters.name: Arnie Pye
characters.description: Springfield's chopper news reporter. Voiced byDan Castellaneta. Deadline News: Occasionally, things go really bad for him while he's in the middle of reporting. In one notable incident, he's about to crash into a mountain during a blizzard just before the (now upside-down) camera cuts off. Deadpan Snarker: When dealing with Kent. Epunymous Title: Originally defied, as his news segment used to be titled "Arnie In The Sky", missing out on the far more obvious pun. Flat Character: Arnie is only Kent'ssnarkychopper reporter and the one time he's in charge shows his characterization is basically the same as Kent's.

characters.name: Barry "Duffman" Duffman
characters.description: Duffman is the mascot and spokesman for Duff Brewing Company. He is an athletic and charismatic figure who is seldom seen without his signature uniform consisting of tights, cape, and a utility belt that holds cans of Duff. Voiced byHank Azaria. Ambiguously Bi: In some episodes Duffman is shown to be gay, but in one of his first appearances it's revealed that he lied to a buxom blonde bartender to get her to sleep with him. He also mentions having two kids and when he was shot by Frank Grimes Jr. he said "I love you, Doris" before losing consciousness. Much like Milhouse, the writers can't seem to decide whether Duffman is straight, gay, or bi, though given that Duffman is a character played by multiple actors, the answer could very well be "all of the above". Catchphrase: "Oh yeah!", usually accompanied by a hip thrust. Expy: Duffman is based on Bud Man, an old mascot and spokesman for Budweiser. His Name Really Is "Barkeep": Lampshaded in "Old Yeller Belly", where when he doesn't have the job anymore, he says he is no longer Duffman, but Barry Duffman.

characters.name: Shauna Tifton A.K.A. Princess Kashmir
characters.description: Princess Kashmir (real name Shauna Tifton) is an exotic dancer. The Cameo: Sometimes. In "Bart After Dark", for example, she appears doing a Fan Dance and dancing with Chief Wiggum in "Homer vs. The Eighteenth Amendment". Hooker with a Heart of Gold: In the episode "Radio Bart", Princess Kashmir is one of the celebrities who volunteer to sing withStingon the song "We're Sending Our Love Down the Well." Hypocrite: In "Homer's Night Out," she says one of her pet peeves is "rude people," but in "Secrets of a Successful Marriage," she is among the Springfielders who eavesdrop on Homer and Marge's dinner. Ms. Fanservice: Chances are, she'll be wearing a skimpy outfit in her appearances.

characters.name: Gil Gunderson
characters.description: Chronically unsuccessful salesman. Voiced byDan Castellaneta. Alliterative Name:GilGunderson. Ascended Extra: Ol' Gil was expected to be aOne-Shot Characterin "Realty Bites". However, Dan Castellaneta was reportedly so funny at that episode's table read, the writers wanted to keep bringing the character back. The retirement of Lionel Hutz also provided an opportunity for Gil to inherit many of his "unlucky businessman" scenes. Attractive Bent-Gender: At least, he was to Moe in "Pray Anything". Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Despite his mostly affable personality, he spends most of his time selling products he knows are faulty and are essentially scams. He also constantly takes advantage of the Simpsons inKill Gil, Volmes I & IIonly to lapse into self-pity whenever they hold him accountable. One episode reveals he shamelessly smuggled drugs inside animatronics in a pizza place.

characters.name: Captain HoratioMcAllister
characters.description: A sea captain and businessman in Springfield. Voiced byHank Azaria. Ambiguously Bi: In one episode he takes glee at being capable of taking a picture of Patty and Selma naked and in another he accepts being handed a handful of dirty magazines while saying that this will prevent his (all-male) crew from having sex with each other out of desperation (but they all look at him when he says this). It's pretty much stated that he becomesway too sex-starved for his own good with his long sea trips. A later episode reveals he has a wife.Flanders:(sighs)Well, Sea Captain, looks like you and I are sailing solo this evening.Sea Captain:Arrrrre you hitting on me?! Because I don't do that. On land. Artificial Limbs: He has an artificial leg. The Drunken Sailor: Was drunk when he crashed a tanker full of oil on Baby Seal Beach in "Bart After Dark". He tries to bribe a reporter on camera to take the blame. Everyone Calls Him "Barkeep": Or rather, everyone calls him the Sea Captain. The episode "New Kid on the Block" is the only time in the series when he is referred to as CaptainMcAllister.

characters.name: Rich Texan
characters.description: A wealthy businessman originally from Texasnoteoriginallyfrom Connecticut. Voiced byDan Castellaneta. Catchphrase: Yeeeeahaw! Corrupt Corporate Executive: He once owned a logging company and once attempted to cut down Springfield's tallest Redwood tree, until his company was destroyed by the gigantic tree after it slid down a hill."Goldarn! I worked hard to ill-get those gains." Everyone Calls Him "Barkeep": Subverted. Rich Texan is hisactual name. He even has a teenaged daughter namedParis Texan. (It helps that "Rich" as a name is short for "Richard".) Fat, Sweaty Southerner in a White Suit: He fits the "fat", "southerner", and "in a white (or, at least, light tan) suit" elements of the trope, though he isn't commonly shown to be sweaty or gluttonous. He is very rich and occasionally somewhat shady.

characters.name: Lindsey Naegle
characters.description: Springfield's residential business link. Voiced byTress MacNeille. The Alcoholic: Is seen in Alcoholics Anonymous on "Days of Wine and D'Oh-ses". Ambiguously Human: In "Day of the Jackanapes", she and an unnamed TV executive turn out to be T-1000 like liquid metal robots. This was never brought up again and it wasn't a Halloween special. Ambiguous Situation: InI Don't Wanna Know Why the Caged Bird SingsMarge has Lindsey on a list of people who she would allow Homer to marry if she ever passed away. What she did to earn this honor is unknown. Ascended Extra: The TV executive that appears in "The Itchy & Scratchy & Poochie Show" and "Girly Edition" behaves, sounds and looks (only with a different hair color) just like her, but she wasn't formally introduced and named until "They Saved Lisa's Brain".

characters.name: Les Moore
characters.description: Santa's Little Helper's original owner who abandoned him on Christmas Eve after his came last too many times. He runs the No Kill Kennel. Voiced byHank Azaria. Bad People Abuse Animals: He cruelly separated Santa's Little Helper from his motherSheBiscuitas a pup then abandoned him on the Springfield Greyhound Racetrack on Christmas Eve just because he kept coming last in every race. Bitch Slap: Receives one from all 5 Simpsons members of The Simpsons family as punishment for his cruelty of Santa's Little Helper. The Bus Came Back: After only appearing the very first episode he reappears in Season 14's Old-Yeller Belly, then reappeared much later in Season 31's The Way of the Dog as the main antagonist. The Dog Bites Back: Santa's Little Helper bites him upon revealing his backstory to him.

characters.name: Cookie Kwan
characters.description: A go-getter in the imploding Springfield real-estate industry, the "number one on the west side". Voiced byTress MacNeille. Asian Rudeness: She is very aggressive toward anyone whom she deems a threat to her business. Asian Speekee Engrish: She has a strong Asian accent even though she grew up in Springfield. A flashback showed she tried to lose it when she was younger, though it clearly didn't take. Catchphrase: She's "number one on the west side". Demoted to Extra: With many of the non-white characters being recast after the murder of George Floyd, both Kwan and Apu have yet to be recast.

characters.name: Roger Meyers, Jr.
characters.description: Owner of Itchy and Scratchy Studios, the makers ofThe Itchy & Scratchy Show, and son of its founder Roger Meyers Sr. Ambiguously Jewish: His last name is Meyers, and he has a long nose and works in entertainment. Ironic, since his father produced a controversial cartoon calledNazi Supermen are Our Superiors. Bad Boss: He treats his employees almost as badly as he treats concerned parents. Especially if they've been to college, andespeciallyif that college is Harvard. Child Hater: To say he has a low opinion of his cartoons' target audience is an understatement. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: He makes no speaking appearances after Season 8, and his reappearance seems less likely after the death of Alex Rocco. He occasionally appears in crowd shots however, cameoing as late as season 36.

characters.name: Hans Moleman
characters.description: A mole-like, heavily wrinkled elderly man with thick glasses andterrible luck, whogets killed a lot. Voiced byDan Castellaneta. The Alcoholic: "Drinking has ruined my life.I'm 31 years old!" Ambiguously Brown: He's sometimes drawn light brown instead of yellow. Blind Without 'Em: And pretty much blind with 'em, too (he is HansMoleman).Hans:(reading a dinner menu) : Cold...biscuits...chicken...yellow...mailman...Waitress:You're reading the wine list, sir.Hans:Very good. Body Horror: If he'sreally31 years old, then alcohol abuse has done anumberon his body.

characters.name: Jasper Beardly
characters.description: A senior citizen in Springfield. Voiced byHarry Shearer. An Arm and a Leg: Has a wooden left leg. Blind Mistake:Jasper:Is this seat taken, little girl?Bart:I'm not a girl. What are you, blind?Jasper:Yes. Butt-Monkey: He has gotten his beard stuck in a pencil sharpener, been frozen alive in one of the Kwik-E-Mart's freezers (on purpose, but it certainly didn't do him any good), turned into a Lorax-like creature after taking the wrong pills, set on fire while lighting the Olympic Flame, andshot in his wooden leg by a drunken Smithers. Characterization Marches On: In "Bart the General", he's Abe's bully who easily takes Abe's newspaper from him and laughs about it. In "Two Cars in Every Garage and Three Eyes on Every Fish", they instead become bickering rivals arguing about who should change the channel. Eventually they're now best friends.

characters.name: Crazy Old Jewish Man
characters.description: He is a friend of Grampa Simpson and Jasper Beardly. Voiced byHank Azaria(Dan Castellanetain "Miracle On Evergreen Terrace"). Accidental Murder: He accidentally killed his uncle while losing control of a ladder. Alter Kocker: Has a strong Yiddish accent and mannerisms. Cloudcuckoolander: Drops his pants and dances the Funky Chicken and sings "Old Grey Mare" for free while Krusty is attempting to get people to pay him. Eventually, he gets on TV with the act and even gets a group of backup singers called "The Crazy Old Man Singers". Dirty Old Man: Has a collection of old sunbathing magazines he loaned to Abe. He's pretty irate when they're destroyed when the retirement home is damaged by Mr. Burns.Abe:Cuz'a [Burns] I lost my home, my things, and my buddy's collection of old sunbathing magazines...Old Jewish Man:Youbastard!

characters.name: Eleanor Abernathy (Crazy Cat Lady)
characters.description: Voiced byTress MacNeille. The Alcoholic: By age 32, she began to feel burned out from her jobs, and started drinking and sought emotional solace with her first cat. Ascended Extra: She debuted relatively early in the Mike Scully era as a one-off joke character and became a recurring character in the Al Jean era, startingsix yearsafter her initial appearance. Black Comedy Animal Cruelty: She sometimes throws her cats at people who make her angry. Brainy Brunette: She was a doctor and lawyer with brown hair before she got burnt out to the point of becoming what she is now.

characters.name: Professor John Frink, Jr.
characters.description: Local mad scientist and nerdy genius. Voiced byHank Azaria. Absent-Minded Professor Ambiguously Jewish: He displays someJewish and Nerdystereotypes and is based on a character played by a Jewish actor; however, he has also been seen in Reverend Lovejoy's church on a few occasions. Belligerent Sexual Tension: Has this with his colleague Prof. Hessler in "FrinkCoin." Bungling Inventor: Several of his inventions have malfunctioned, with hilarious results.

characters.name: Disco Stu
characters.description: The owner of Stu's Disco and a huge fan of Disco music. Voiced byHank Azaria. Abusive Parents: Both his parents shame him for his love of Disco,while they have similar musical obsessions like doo-wop and public domain music. Ambiguously Bi: In one episode, he claims to be "heteroflexible", but Smithers thinks he’s only going through a phase and Stu himself has only been shown romantically involved with women. Ambiguously Christian: The Pope apparently had the authority to annul his marriage to Selma, and in fact did so. Ascended Extra: Originally appeared as a punchline to the fact that Homer's old jacket said "Disco Stu" when it should have said "Disco Stud", he has since become one of the show's most memorable characters.

characters.name: Just Stamp the Ticket Man
characters.description: ADeadpan Snarkerwho appears sporadically throughout the series. Voiced byHank Azaria. The Artifact:Word of Godsays they never use him anymore because they have Raphael to fill any role in an episode he could have filled. Catchphrase: "Just stamp the ticket" and "You sicken me". Deadpan Snarker: He'll often appear just to make a smart remark. Fisticuff-Provoking Comment: He often punches people that annoy him, notably Homer.

characters.name: The Yes Guy (Frank Nelson-Type)
characters.description: An eccentric Springfield worker. Voiced byDan Castellaneta. Catchphrase: "EEE-Yeeeeeeeeesssss?" Large Ham: He talks the way he does because he had a stroke. Nice Guy: Is unflinchingly courteous and helpful. No Celebrities Were Harmed: As you might guess, he's based upon actor Frank Nelson in his appearances onThe Jack Benny Show,I Love Lucy, andSanford & Son.

characters.name: Bleeding Gums Murphy
characters.description: A blues musician in Springfield. Voiced by Ron Taylor andKevin Michael Richardson. Abusive Parents: Or Abusive Uncle in his case.Turns out that he was one of theseto his own nephew, in a passive-aggressive, backhanded way. As in,he constantly complimented Lisa around him and declared him not as good.However, this is not the case with his son, to whom he cared for deeply. Back for the Dead: In "'Round Springfield". Dead Artists Are Better: Upon hearing of his death, Comic Book Guy doubles the already steep price he's asking for a copy ofSax On The Beach. Drunk on Milk: In his backstory, he became pretty rich from his one studio record but he lost it all with an obsession to buy Faberge eggs that (in the flashback) is portrayed similar to alcoholism.

characters.name: Squeaky-Voiced Teen
characters.description: An anxious teenager working many menial jobs in Springfield. Voiced byDan Castellaneta. Butt-Monkey: Tends to work demeaning jobs. Casanova Wannabe: His other defining characteristic, aside from his squeaky voice and working sucky retail jobs. He's always seen hitting on, attempting to hit on, or otherwise doing something to attract girls. At times he will lament his lack of success or virginity,despite actually not having that bad of a success rate. His Name Really Is "Barkeep": "Full Heart, Empty Pool" suggests that his name is "Andrew Teen". I Have No Son!: On the receiving end from Lunchlady Doris when he was unable to let her bowl at the Bowl-a-Rama.

characters.name: Raphael (Sarcastic Clerk, Wiseguy)
characters.description: A wisecracking clerk. Voiced byHank Azaria. Arms Dealer: InThe Cartridge Family, he runs a gun shop. Ascended Extra: He evolved from a funny voice Hank Azaria used for miscellaneous bit characters into a fully fledged character. Deadpan Snarker: His main trait is adding a sarcastic remark in any situation. Depending on the Artist: Either has gray or black hair, depending on the episode.

characters.name: Artie Ziff
characters.description: Marge's secondLove Interestwhom she found disgusting for hisNo Sense of Personal Spaceadvances on her. Ever since their break up, Artie managed to hit it big in life but still holds a fervent torch for Marge after all these years. Abhorrent Admirer: To Marge, who found him disgusting. He doesn’t help his case by trying to forcing himself into her during their prom date. Ascended Extra: He appears for the first time in "The Way We Was" as a minor character of the Homer and Marge flashback. Later, he becomes the main focus in "Half-Decent Proposal", "The Ziff Who Came to Dinner" and "Hail to the Teeth". Bolivian Army Ending: During the end of "The Ziff Who Came To Dinner", while upon being incarcerated, he begins spraying the cigarettes of all the fellow inmates. As an angry mob grows around him,Marge sadly tells the family to take one last look at Artie. This would be his last appearance (barring flashback and non-canon appearances) until hereturnedin "Hail to the Teeth". Broken Ace: He's a charismatic, tech-savvy, self-made billionaire, yet has spent years pining after a woman who rejected him after a single date.

characters.name: Sam and Larry
characters.description: The two barflies at Moe's Tavern. Voiced byHarry ShearerandHank Azaria. The Alcoholic: They are almost always seen drunk. Flat Character: Virtually nothing is known about either of them.Played for Dramawith Larry as Homer and his friends left so little impression that they made up a story at his funeral, and feel guilty for never knowing him. Gasshole: InTapped Out, Larry's unlock message is a burp. Promotion to Opening Titles: Sam gets added to the house pan shot in season 2, but is removed in the HD intro.

characters.name: Patches & Poor Violet
characters.description: Two poor orphan siblings. Voiced byPamela HaydenandTress MacNeille. Heartwarming Orphan: Mocked to high heaven. In a more regular show someone would have taken pity on these poor creatures a long time ago, but in a place like Springfield they are just one more cog in a machine of endless misery. Pauper Patches: One of them is evennamed Patches. Street Urchin: They even look like they came out ofOliver Twistand quote the book's most famous line on their recruitment inThe Simpsons: Tapped Out. Tiny Tim Template: Lisa introduces these sickly orphans to Bart, who give him a ragged one dollar bill they had been saving when everyone at their orphanage heard what had happened, which unfortunately does not help his extreme guilt over the truth. When the truth does get out, the orphan duo are just as furious as the rest of the townsfolk, as the dollar they gave Bart was their vitamin money.

characters.name: Miss Springfield
characters.description: Miss Springfield is a beauty pageant winner and the secret wife of Mayor Quimby. Voiced byPamela Hayden. Brainless Beauty: She is very cute, but also dumb and illiterate. Once mistook Quimby's sash saying 'Mayor' for 'Major' and thought he was in the army. Cute, but Cacophonic: In "Mr. Spritz Goes to Washington", Mayor Quimby redirects airplane traffic away from the motel where he conducts his affairs so he can hear her voice. When he discovers that she falls under this trope, Quimby laments "Now I regret buying you that opera house!". Dumb Blonde: A classic example. Bad voice, can't read, only kept around by Quimby for the sex. Even in the episode where Lisa was discriminated against because of her hair color, she demonstrates her intelligence, further reinforcing this stereotype in front of Lisa herself. The Mistress: She is the official lover of Mayor Quimbly and has been seen in bed with him several times.

characters.name: Benjamin, Doug and Gary
characters.description: Nerdy college students at Springfield University who help Homer study nuclear physics. Voiced byDan Castellaneta,Hank Azaria, andHarry Shearer. All There in the Manual: Their names, with the exception of Gary, aren't stated onscreen, only mentioned in the original episode guide, and even there, it's unclear who was who. Big, Thin, Short Trio: Doug (fat), Gary (tall and thin), Benjamin (short). Black and Nerdy: Gary. Geek Physiques: Benjamin and Gary are skinny, Doug is fat.

characters.name: Declan Desmond
characters.description: British documentary filmmaker. Voiced byEric Idle. Alliterative Name:DeclanDesmond. Jerkass: He demeans everyone he talks to.Jerkass Has a Point: His criticism of Lisa's "buffet style" intellectualism and suggestion that she pick a road and stick to it helps her to focus on her goals. Jerkass Has a Point: His criticism of Lisa's "buffet style" intellectualism and suggestion that she pick a road and stick to it helps her to focus on her goals. No Celebrities Were Harmed: Sounds just like David Attenborough.

characters.name: Julio Franco
characters.description: ACamp Gayrecurring character. Voiced byHank Azaria(2003-2021)/Tony Rodriguez (2021-present) All Gays are Promiscuous: He and Smithers break up when Smithers refuses to meet his demand for a boyfriend who's 20% loyal to him. Always Camp: In "The Blue and the Gray," he works as Marge's hairdresser. Camp Gay: He is shown to be very flamboyant. Expy: He is based on Azaria's similarly flamboyantCamp Gaycharacter Agador fromThe Birdcage, which also initially made him a case ofInk-Suit Actor.

characters.name: Jebediah Springfield
characters.description: The legendary founder of Springfield. Voiced byHarry Shearer(Hank Azariain "McMansionand Wife"). "Lisa The Iconoclast" turned him into Hans Sprungfeld, a vile pirate who created Springfield for his own selfish means. This character detail has since largely been ignored in future episodes. Been There, Shaped History: Parodied. In "Lisa The Iconoclast", he was apparently the reason for why the famous portrait of George Washington is missing the lower half, having attacked the man while it was being painted, and as he limped away stood on the painting, ripping it and taking part of the painting with him, which he used to write a confession. Everyone Has Standards: Though the city he fathered isn't the most moral by any means, he seemed to have a set of standards, given that he and half of his fellow settlers were appalled by Shelbyville Manhattan's wanting to have a law on marrying cousins. This is later retconned intoEven Evil Has Standardsonce the writers turned him into a pirate criminal. Historical Hero Upgrade: A one-off thing for "Lisa The Iconoclast". Went down in town legend as having tamed a wild buffalo. As his confessional reveals, it had actually been perfectly tame whenhe shot it. Meaningful Name:Although the name Jebediah was made up for the show, it can be back-constructed into the Hebrew form יבדיהו (Yivdayahu), which actually has a meaning in Hebrew: "God will fabricate"noteSpecifically, thetriconsonantal rootב-ד-ה, which means "fiction".. Very appropriate for someone whose persona as a heroic pioneer is completely made up.

characters.name: Ian
characters.description: A very tall man. Voiced byHank Azaria. The Alleged Car: Implied with his VW Bug — it works perfectly fine (that we can see), but he barely fits in and he points out to Nelson that it's the biggest car he could afford. Author Avatar: He's based in appearance and name off one of the show's writers, the 6'8 Ian Maxtone-Graham. Beware the Nice Ones: He actually seems like a very pleasant guy, so long as you don't make fun of his height. The Big Guy: He's not only very tall, he's also implied to be very strong, being able to pick Nelson up with just one hand and intimidate him into being laughed at by the other townsfolk.The Simpsons Guide To Springfieldalso shows he's a regular patron of "Royal Majesty For The Obese Or Gangly Gentleman", a tailor shop that specializes in custom clothing for very fat and/or tall men.

characters.name: The Vanderbilts
characters.description: An elderly rich couple who are frequently shocked by Homer's antics. Voiced byHank AzariaandTress MacNeille. Catchphrase: Mrs. Vanderbilt tends to say "Oh, good heavens!" when she sees something shocking. High-Class Glass: Mr. Vanderbilt wears a monocle. It typically falls off. Preppy Name: Their name is recognizable as one of the most famous upperclass families of the Gilded Age.

characters.name: Maya
characters.description: A little adult who dates Moe after meeting him online.Later on, they become anOfficial Couplein "The Wayz We Were."Voiced byTress MacNeille. The Bus Came Back: Returns in "The Wayz We Were". Dude, Not Funny!: When Moe suddenly starts saying too many little people jokes, it causes Maya to leave him. Huge Guy, Tiny Girl: Next to Moe's Huge Guy. Nice Girl: An overall nice woman.

characters.name: Michael "Mike" Wegman
characters.description: An intern at the Power Plant who idolizes Homer, as Homer is always at the center of attention (for better or worse, mostly the latter). Voiced byMichael Rapaport. Berserk Button: Anyone criticizing Homer will result in Mike dishing out rants to them. Bullying a Dragon: After Mr. Burns criticized Homer, Mike goes on a long rant telling how much Mr. Burns sucks. This earns Mike a bullet shot (thankfully, he survives because the gun was pretty old). Can't Take Criticism: Homer getting criticism is what Mikecan'thandle to see. Fatal Flaw: Hisinability to handle Homer being criticized. He tends to deliver a long rant to anyone, including Bart, who insults Homer. This has gotten him in trouble, withMargedemanding him and his wife out of the Simpsons' household for making Bart cry and getting shot in the face by Mr. Burns, which would've killed him if not for the gun being old.

characters.name: Pharm Team Scientists
characters.description: A pair of pharmacists who develop various pharmaceutical drugs and medications for the Pharm Team research lab. Voiced byHank AzariaandTress MacNeille. Expy: The male pharmacist is modeled after Lewis Skolnick, the nerdy protagonist fromRevenge of the Nerds. No Name Given: Neither one has received any names since their debut. Suspiciously Similar Substitute: To Professor Frink and Lindsey Naegle, not least thanks to having the same voice actors between them all. Those Two Guys: They're always seen together.

characters.name: Truth-Anne
characters.description: Academic Alpha Bitch: Passive-Aggressive variant. Establishing Character Moment: She is playing in her principal's office when Bart and Skinner visit the latter to discuss peace between their schools. But when Bart realizes the principal is not the one in charge, Truth-Anne's playful expression changes to a stoic one while telling the principal to leave them. Wise Beyond Their Years: Downplayed. She's about the same age as Bart, but runs a Montessori School and has enough authority to fire an employee.

characters.name: Kang and Kodos
characters.description: Brother and sister (respectively) cyclopian aliens resembling giant green heads on writhing octopus tentacles, these two aliens from Rigel IV make guest appearances in some episodes but are most prominent in theTreehouse of Horrorepisodes, which are non-canonical horror anthologies. Voiced byHarry ShearerandDan Castellaneta. Affably Evil: Crosses over withBenevolent Boss. One comic had them abduct all the right-handed people on Earth (or at least in Springfield) to make clothing for them, but they are pretty lax bosses who treat their workers nicely. Depending on the writer, they can be pleasant at times. Aliens Are Bastards: Subverted in their initial appearance, though their later appearances tend to parody this. Aliens Speaking English: Rigellian coincidentally sounds just like English.

characters.name: Blinky the Three-Eyed Fish
characters.description: Expy: A crow with three eyes begins to make appearances later, presumably the same one that'sfrequently heard outside the power plant. It serves essentially the same role Blinky does. Extra Eyes: Has three eyes. Assumed by most to be the result of the power plant's radiation. Fish People: A one-off gag has an orange, three-eyed Gill-man emerge from water and attack someone. Promotion to Opening Titles: He gets added to the house pan shot in the HD intro. Running Gag: A living one.

characters.name: God
characters.description: Voiced byHarry Shearer. Berserk Button: He apparently is displeased of Reverend Lovejoy, likely due to being apathetic to Ned Flanders' beliefs. The Faceless: His face is obscured by blinding light, although there's a definiteGrandpa Godvibe. Though His face was briefly seen in the opening of "Treehouse of Horror XVI". Final Boss: OfThe Simpsons Game, fought in a round of aDanceDanceRevolution-like mini-game. God: The Almighty Ruler and creator of the Universe.

characters.name: Bender Bending Rodriguez
characters.description: Voiced byJohn DiMaggio. A loudmouthed, kleptomaniac, misanthropic robot currently residing in the Simpsons' basement. He initially made cameo appearances in multiple episodes until he (and the rest of the cast ofFuturama) have a major role inSimpsorama. He still makes occasional appearances whenever events affect the Simpsons household itself, such asthe basement getting flooded. He has his own pageherefor Futurama-related stories. The Alcoholic: Played with. Bender runs on beer, so he is seen occasionally drinking and Homer is aware of this enough that he feeds Bender beer while he is hibernating.

characters.name: Season  31
characters.description: A young charismatic new preacher who becomes the new minister of the church after leaving Michigan. Broken Pedestal: When the people of Springfield find out he burned a Bible as an object lesson the base is broken on forgiving him for it. He's ultimately ousted. Magnetic Hero: His charisma comes from interpreting his faith to seek harmony instead of division. He maintains no prejudices or judgements for people's differences, emulating the omnibenevolent love God is said to have. My Greatest Failure: Burning a Bible as an object lesson that it's just a material object and nothing worth people dividing and judging each other over. Nice Guy: Bode is a mellow guy who never raises his voice and avoids conflict.

characters.name: Season  32
characters.description: A former TV star who dated Grampa.

characters.name: Season  33
characters.description: Big Bad: Of the 2-partA Serious Flandersspecial. The Dreaded: Every Simpsons character who comes across him thinks he's terrifying, and for very good reason. Expy: He's not a full-onCaptain Ersatz, but the general cut of his character is taken from Lorne Malvo from season 1 ofFargo; an erudite but utterly vicious assassin with a knack for monologues. Genre Refugee: He's a character who would fit snugly in the dark world ofFargo; significantly less so inThe Simpsons, which results in the master assassin having to accommodate to theQuirky Town. This is lampooned about as far as it will go, complete with Kostas having aRunning Gagwhere he tries to break into one ofFargo's trademark monologues, only for him to be repeatedly interrupted. Knight of Cerebus: The episode is a take onFargoand Kostas is in the role ofMalvo. While he's definitely not immune to comedy, overall, Kostas has fewer comedic moments than any of the other villains and completely lacks redeeming qualities.

characters.name: Season  34
characters.description: The adopted grandson of Blythe, a woman Grampa dates. Broken Pedestal: While he takes it well, he's horrified to see how his doting father figure treats his actual son. Morality Pet: A one-time occurrence for Abe, who feels like he failed too hard to try with Homer and knows Bart and Lisa don't trustDoting Parents, so he tries to be super gentle with this new kid. You Remind Me of X:Played for Drama, as Homer can't understand why Abe isn't eating this "weird kid" alive whenhewas a weird kid and Abe hated him.

characters.name: Season  35
characters.description: The founder and CEO of the Lifeboat company. Owner of the Macweldon Distillery and patriarch of the Macweldon family.

characters.name: Season  36
characters.description: Krusty the Clown's aunt who (supposedly) fixes relationship problems, but in reality, is a verbally abusive and mean-spirited woman. Asshole Victim: Played with. By the end of her debut episode, Sadie gets crushed to death by the sign of her show,The Problem is You. On one hand, the viewers would feel bad for her. But on the other hand, given her harsh treatment of everyone throughout the episode (particularly Krusty and Marge), it's hard to muster sympathy for the lady. Dropped a Bridge on Him: More like a huge sign. While Sadie is rambling on about how everybody needs her, Drederick Tatum's pet tiger accidentally loosens the rope to the show's sign with its tail, causing the sign to fall and squash Sadie flat. Hate Sink:Jerkass Has a Pointaside, she boils nuanced relationships down to one problem only, and those points are delivered in a way that makes the problem haver feel as defensive as possible. Jerkass Has a Point: She's not wrong in her criticisms of the main characters; Marge loves being a martyr with others dependent on her, Krusty is an awful boss, and Homer/Patty/Selma are more alike than they think; she just delivers all the points as harsh and one-note as possible.

characters.name: Season  37
characters.description: Veterinarian/nutritionist at the St. Bernard of Assisi Medical Center and is also the dog trainer for various dog shows, who helps Marge get Santa's Little Helper back into shape, but, is actually a treasure hunter who plans to use the dog to find Benjamin Franklin's stolen treasure. Arch-Enemy: Serves as this to Marge for taking away Santa's Little Helper from her. Big Bad: Of the episode. Corrupted Character Copy: Of Adrian Pennino from theRockyfranchise. Fallen Hero: She seems nice to Marge and SLH at first by helping slim SLH back to his original shape and helping Marge win competitons and dog shows with him, but, it turns that she was using her to find the stolen treasure of Benjamin Franklin with said dog.

characters.name: Russ Cargill
characters.description: The power-mad Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), he decides to take drastic action against Springfield when the nearby lake's pollution reaches a critical level, trapping the entire city under a glass dome to contain the toxic waste. At Least I Admit It: Upon learning that the Simpsons have escaped the dome and that Homer is responsible for polluting the lake in the first place, Cargill orders one of his men to capture the Simpsons at all costs and have them placed back inside the dome. He also declares that he wants death squads surrounding the dome to ensure that no one else gets in or out. The man replies that Cargill has gone mad with power, to which Cargill admits to without surprise.EPA Employee: Sir, I'm afraid you've gone mad with power.Cargill:Of course, I have. You ever tried going mad without power? It's boring, no one listens to you. Anvil on Head: He's defeated when Maggie knocks him out by (somehow) pushing a boulder on top of his head. Bad Boss: After the Simpsons manage to escape the dome, he angrily throws his binoculars at a nearby aide, who dodges them. Karma immediately bites him in the ass as they bounce back from the dome and into his eyes. Big Bad: He's the main antagonist ofThe Simpsons Movie.

characters.name: President Schwarzenegger
characters.description: Arnold Schwarzeneggeris portrayed as thePresident of the United StatesinThe Simpsons Movie. He signs off on Cargill's plan to contain Springfield with a giant dome. The Ahnold: Sort of. He's a parody of Arnold Schwarzenegger (much like Rainier Wolfcastle, whom Harry Shearer also voices); though instead of aNo Celebrities Were Harmedexpy, he's literally supposed to be Schwarzenegger himself. Artistic License – Politics: In real life, Schwarzenegger can't be the U.S. President due to not being a natural-born citizen (in fact, the actual Schwarzenegger is Austrian). Character Development:Slightly. After his blind choosing of the plan to seal Springfield in a dome leads to a disaster, Schwarzenegger declares he needs to read what he's approving when Cargill presents him with a solution to the dome problem. Too bad Cargill manipulates him into blindly choosing the option to nuke Springfield instead. Convenient Replacement Character: For Rainier Wolfcastle, right down to sharing the same physical appearance, mannerisms, and voice actor.

characters.name: Plopper
characters.description: Absent Animal Companion: Although his appearances in the series followingThe Moviehave mostly been limited to the oddcameoaround Springfield, "Pork and Burns," an episode released ten years after the movie, shows that he still belongs to the Simpsons.Because Marge does all the work of caring for him, his existence barely affects the rest of the family.Bart:We have a pig? Fuzz Therapy: In "Pork and Burns," Homer fakes an anxiety disorder so that he can get a prescription for a therapy animal, enabling him to take Plopper anywhere he wants. It soon becomes clear thatPlopper actually does serve the function of a therapy animal to Homer, helping him to regulate his emotions and overall making him a happier and more even-keeled person. Housepet Pig: Homer decides to take this pig home after seeing him in a TV ad for Krusty Burger, wanting tosave him from being slaughteredon Krusty's orders. Meaningful Name: His manure production nearly spelled doom for Springfield. Messy Pig: Plopper produces ahugeamount of feces in a short span of time, which Homer stores in an overflowing silo.

characters.name: Colin
characters.description: An Irish boy in Springfield who befriends Lisa. Birds of a Feather: He and Lisa immediately hit it off due to their shared love of environmentalism. Never Heard That One Before: Being Irish and an environmentalist, he isn't surprised when Lisa asks ifBonois his dad. Nice Guy: Colin's a cordial, friendly person. He's notably one of the few Springfielders who doesn't try to kill the Simpson family after Homer gets them trapped in the dome. Oireland: He's an Irish immigrant.

characters.name: Medicine Woman
characters.description: Boob-Based Gag: Her large, sagging breasts are the reason that Homer ends up calling her "Boob Lady". When Homer gets lost trying to find his way from Alaska back to Springfield, he sees a vision of her in the sky in which she sways her boobs to point in the direction that he's meant to go. The Cameo: Appears in the opening sequence directly following the movie and makes a brief speaking cameo in "Boy Meets Curl", wherein Homer refers to her as his therapist and the two have a... "session" together. Magical Native American: An Inuit version. No Name Given: Despite her rather notable role in the movie, her name never gets mentioned.

characters.name: Season  1
characters.description: She is the fourth grade teacher at the "Enriched Learning Center for Gifted Children" that Bart briefly attended after cheating on an intelligence test. Foil: She is calm and nurturing to her students and encourages independence and creativity in a pedagogically progressive environment, which heavily contrasts Mrs. Krabappel. Howard is the cool kid at Noiseland Video Arcade who teaches Homer how to beat Bart at video-game boxing. Cool Shades: He wears sunglasses. Almighty Mom: Even Homer is scolded by her for playing video games with little children.

characters.name: Season  2
characters.description: Karl is a former diehard assistant of Homer. Foil: To Smithers. Both are personal assistants to executives at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant (Karl for Homer, Smithers for Burns). But while Smithers grovels to Mr. Burns and enables his worst interests, Karl empowers Homer and helps him grow into being a better man. Heroic Sacrifice: When Homer is exposed for using the company's health plan to buy the Dimoxinil for his hair, Karl takes the fall to avoid Homer getting fired. I Just Want My Beloved to Be Happy: He takes the fall when Homer is exposed for insurance fraud because he loves Homer enough to take a bullet. Straight Gay: Although it is never directly said, it is been suggested that Karl is homosexual. There are many indications as he kisses Homer during his pep talk and explains, "My mother taught me never to kiss a fool" before slapping Homer's buttocks.

characters.name: Season  3
characters.description: Leon is a mental patient who acts like Michael Jackson. The Bus Came Back:Leon makes an appearance inMr. Lisa's Opus, 26 years after his debut, once again singing a happy birthday song to Lisa.If one counts the Bongo Comics as canon, he also reappeared in 1997's issue 31, playing Fallout Boy to Homer's Radioactive Man (Homer took a blow to the head and believed he was the real Radioactive Man, Leon played along for fun). Leon makes an appearance inMr. Lisa's Opus, 26 years after his debut, once again singing a happy birthday song to Lisa. If one counts the Bongo Comics as canon, he also reappeared in 1997's issue 31, playing Fallout Boy to Homer's Radioactive Man (Homer took a blow to the head and believed he was the real Radioactive Man, Leon played along for fun). But Now I Must Go: He leaves town after revealing he's not really Michael Jackson.

characters.name: Season  4
characters.description: The camp director of Kamp Krusty. Bad Boss: Mr. Black does very little work, instead relying on the services of the school bullies Jimbo Jones, Dolph and, Kearney, who run the "Kamp Krusty" with an iron fist, to "crush their spirits". Card-Carrying Villain: He gives a toast saying "Gentlemen, to evil!" Faux Affably Evil: He never raises his voice and always acts in a professional, if boring, dour and soulless, way. He's still aCard-Carrying Villainwho revels in his evil. Karma Houdini: Aside from the camp being overthrown, he and his cronies appear to face no real repercussions for their actions (although aside from a few appearances in the comics, Mr. Black never appears again in the series).

characters.name: Season  5
characters.description: The agent who signed the Be Sharps to a record deal and managed them during their 15 minutes of fame. No Celebrities Were Harmed: He's a mix of bothThe Beatles' manager Brian Epstein and their producer George Martin. Snake Oil Salesman: As per Lisa, he's just selling a bunch of easy answers. An attractive new employee at the power plant, Homer quickly develops a strong attraction to her, which is compounded by the revelation of their many similarities and the two being sent on a business trip together. Ambiguous Situation: More episodes later, Homer mentions that Mindy became an alcoholic and lost her job at the plant after his time with her, but future episodes "Team Homer" and "The Twisted World of Marge Simpson" show Mindy as sober and working at the plant.

characters.name: Season  6
characters.description: Birch Barlow is a right-wing conservative talk show host on the radio station KBBL. He also has a show on Fox News. Fat Bastard: He's very rotund and very abrasive to anyone who doesn't fit with his political beliefs. Irony: One of his favourite points to go after Quimby about is his stance on crime. But Birch is aiding a felon in the form of the attempted murderer Sideshow Bob. One that he helped free from jail, no less. Jerkass Has a Point: He's an unpleasant man to talk to unless you align with him politically, but he's absolutely right regarding his criticisms of Quimby, if nothing else. Meaningful Name: "Birch" is likely meant to be a reference to the infamousJohn Birch Society, a radical conservative/conspiracy theory group formed during the 1950s.

characters.name: Season  7
characters.description: Cartoonish Supervillainy: He is the partialTrope Namer. While in his jail cell he tries to activate his "Colosso-boots", and slams his head against the ceiling, leaving him to sigh and ask when his lawyer's showing up. A Day in the Limelight: The comics give him a one-off story showing him trying to be a supervillain, and just how bad he is at it. Epic Fail: He's a supervillain so bad Chief Wiggum can catch and contain him.Chief Wiggum.In the comics, meanwhile, he's so ineffectual Wiggum doesn't even think he's worth arresting, no matter how much property damage he causes. A pig that Homer imagines during his imagination of his weight goal. No Celebrities Were Harmed: He is based onCary Grant. The creators even wanted Grant to play the pig until they remembered he'd been dead for years.

characters.name: Season  8
characters.description: The president of the Globex Corporation, which includes a rival nuclear power plant. He tried to entice Smithers with an offer to switch jobs, and when Smithers turned it down, the same offer was quickly made to the next longest-serving employee of the Springfield plant: Homer. As a boss, he's everything Burns is not: friendly, outgoing, hip, and concerned about his employees. He's also a Bond villain. Easily one of the most popular one-off characters. Affably Evil: Polite, benevolent to his employees to the point that they're his number two concern (number one being his schemes), and all in all a great guy to hang around with. He's also a supervillain. Ax-Crazy: Especially in the episode's climax. The Bad Guy Wins:Successfully takes over the East Coast. Though given his personality it may not be too bad. Beard of Evil: He has a beard, and he is evil.

characters.name: Season  9
characters.description: TherealSeymour Skinner. He was a sergeant in the US Army, but got caught by the enemy and spent five years in a POW camp, and was then sold to a shoe-producing company in China. After the company closed, he came back to Springfield, only to find out that Armin Tamzarian basically lived his life for the entire time he was gone.
